title: Private deployment activation heatmap and cross-team commitment framework
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Produce a one-page quarterly plan (activation heatmap) that maps customer cohorts, release windows, technical compatibility risk, and cross-team commitments (Eng/Support/SEs/Security). This artifact will be used in exec review and for sprint commitments. Scope includes defining leading indicators, thresholds for go/no-go, and a lightweight commitment SLA for each team for the Q2 private/VPC/on‑prem rollout wave.
comments: 2025-11-10 - Aisha Patel: Draft ticket created after exec sync. Need to align on the heatmap dimensions: (customer cohort, compatibility risk, data sensitivity, ops readiness). Suggested stakeholders: Eng (Runtime/Deploy), Security, Solutions, Customer Success, Sales Engineering.

2025-11-12 - Liam Chen: Scheduled alignment workshop with Eng leads 2025-11-17. Proposal: use a 3x3 risk x readiness grid and map customers into tranche lanes. Will prototype a sample heatmap for 6 pilot customers.

2025-11-17 - Priya Rao (Engineering): Workshop notes — Eng prefers mechanical signals (integration tests passing, latency delta < 15%, infra checklist green) while SEs want account-level acceptance (customer infra validation). Trade-off: account-level checks increase gating friction but reduce risk. Action: implement account-level checklist as an opt-in verification step for high-security cohorts.

2025-11-19 - Marco Alvarez (Security): Security review required for any on-prem package. We need a KMS/HSM checklist and upgrade migration plan. Security will provide a baseline questionnaire by 2025-11-24.

2025-11-20 - Liam Chen: Uploaded prototype heatmap to Confluence and created PR to update private deploy runbook. Links below. Next step: map current committed customers and identify 10 highest-risk accounts for mitigation planning.
acceptance_criteria: One-page heatmap artifact in Confluence that covers all Q2 private/VPC/on‑prem customers with visual lanes for cohort, risk, and ops-readiness
Cross-team commitment matrix signed off by Eng, Security, Solutions, and CS with explicit acceptance criteria for each lane
List of leading indicators (>=6 signals) with numeric thresholds and a 'yellow' early-warning definition
Runbook updates (private-deploy-runbook v2) that document measurables and the opt-in account verification flow
Rollout gating decisions can be made using the heatmap and commit matrix without additional ad-hoc exec input
notes: Heatmap axes proposal: X-axis = Technical Compatibility Risk (Low/Medium/High), Y-axis = Ops Readiness (Green/Amber/Red). Cohorts layered by data sensitivity tier.

Leading indicators to include: CI pass rate on customer infra matrix, observed latency delta (baseline vs on‑prem), error-rate spike post-deploy, support ticket open rate within 72 hours, security questionnaire completeness, upgrade-test success rate.

Commitment framework: each team must declare a 'capacity band' for the quarter (low/medium/high) and a primary owner for escalation. Example: Eng commit = 2 triage engineers reserved for high-risk activations; Solutions commit = 1 SE per 5 customers for onboarding; CS commit = 3-week readiness window for pre-activation checklist.

Risks & mitigations: If latency delta > 20% we will automatically shift customer to a canary region until optimizations complete. If security questionnaire incomplete beyond 14 days, activation is paused and SEs will request a customer LOE to progress.
Plan to surface the heatmap weekly in the Private deploy sync and to wire 3 Grafana panels into the artifact for live signals.
